commits.edited_message:
alpha_dec: decode all alpha rows in one pass when dithering is on

VP8DecompressAlphaRows() decoded the alpha plane one macroblock row at
a time even when alpha dithering was going to reprocess the whole plane
afterwards. When dithering is enabled, request all remaining rows in
one pass instead: the pre-processing flag says nothing about the row
schedule, so stop keying the decision on it.

Change-Id: I723363f8ac482cd2419c585c68f6fb468a54926d

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

use sliding window for decoded alpha rows

Allocate only a sliding output row window for dec->alpha_plane in
AllocateMemory (frame_dec.c) when alpha dithering is not active. The
full plane is only reserved when dequantizing the levels will actually
do something, i.e. when the alpha header marks them as pre-processed.

Change-Id: I2a32c3ed493f6e097e573cf5cf0de8a9c96fcfae

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The defect is a disagreement about what 'alpha dithering is active' means, introduced half in each of the two edited commits; neither diff is wrong on its own.

- Commit 48ef187 (edited; 'alpha_dec: decode all alpha rows in one pass when dithering is on') keeps only the alpha_dec.c half of the original change: VP8DecompressAlphaRows() now requests the whole plane in one pass whenever dec->alpha_dithering > 0, and the alpha-header pre-processing gate that the original commit had moved into VP8InitDithering() (frame_dec.c) is not introduced, so dec->alpha_dithering stays the plain clamped user option. At this point in history AllocateMemory() still allocates pic_hdr.width * pic_hdr.height alpha bytes unconditionally, so a one-pass decode always fits: this commit is memory-safe and behaves as its message says.
- Commit 3e2b0b4 (edited; 'use sliding window for decoded alpha rows') makes AllocateMemory() size dec->alpha_plane from WebPGetAlphaWindowRows(), which returns the full crop height only when dithering applies, re-deriving that from the ALPH header pre-processing bits instead of from dec->alpha_dithering, and otherwise returns a ~216-row sliding window (VP8LGetWindowRows). The new gate is redundant/equivalent while VP8InitDithering() still zeroes dec->alpha_dithering for unpreprocessed streams, so this commit alone is also memory-safe and matches its message.

Composed, the two definitions diverge for an in-contract input: a lossy WebP carrying an uncompressed ALPH chunk whose header byte marks pre_processing=0 while the caller passes options.alpha_dithering_strength=100 (a documented 0..100 option). Sizing sees dithering_applies==0 and allocates the 216-row window; the decode-time one-pass still keys off dec->alpha_dithering>0 and makes ALPHDecode() write all 1024 rows through WebPUnfilters[WEBP_FILTER_NONE] (memcpy per row) into that window - a heap-buffer-overflow write 0 bytes past the end of the 20361-byte dec->mem allocation (ASan, rc 134), reached from the public WebPDecode() on line VP8DecompressAlphaRows -> ALPHDecode.

Why the fix is non-local: reverting either single edit removes the crash (with only 48ef187's edit the plane is always full-height; with only 3e2b0b4's edit VP8InitDithering's gate has already zeroed dec->alpha_dithering, so window sizing and the row schedule agree), and each diff read in isolation is consistent with its own commit message - the bug exists only as the mismatch between the sizing condition introduced by 3e2b0b4 (alpha_dec.c WebPGetAlphaWindowRows) and the row-schedule condition left by 48ef187 (alpha_dec.c VP8DecompressAlphaRows feeding on the ungated flag from frame_dec.c VP8InitDithering). Detecting or repairing it requires comparing the two commits: a correct fix must make both sites derive 'dithering is active' the same way (align the one-pass condition with the header-derived condition used for sizing, or restore the init-time gate), which spans both edited commits' code.

pocs.entry_point: WebPDecode (webp/decode.h): probe encodes a 64x1024 lossy frame with the public WebPEncodeRGB(), rewraps it at runtime into a VP8X+ALPH+VP8 container whose ALPH header selects method=0/filter=none/pre_processing=0, then decodes it back through the public WebPDecode() with WebPDecoderConfig.options.alpha_dithering_strength=100 and MODE_RGBA output
